si_4_title.answer: Fractionating autism based on neuroanatomical normative modeling

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Gaussian process regression (GPR) was used to predict vertex-wise cortical thickness.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Gaussian process regression (GPR) was used to estimate a normative model of CT across the cortical surface

nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: we focused on cortical thickness (CT) because firstly, alterations in CT have been extensively reported in different autism studies and secondly, it is a reliable measure of cortical morphology in autism

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age, sex, full-scale IQ (FIQ), Freesurfer Euler number, and dummy coded site variables.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: GPR was trained on the NT cohort (N=206) using the following covariates (i.e. independent variables): age, sex, full-scale IQ (FIQ), the Freesurfer Euler number indicating the topological complexity of the reconstructed cortical surface and which has been validated as a surrogate marker for image quality, plus dummy coded variables representing data acquisition sites.
